---
title: "Step 2b. Select one image per sequence (by-image test set)"
output: html_document
---

## Purpose

Build the image-level ("by image") version of the `awt_2026_11` test set: the same
2,905 validated sequences, one image each. The by-sequence set scores a sequence on
up to two random images, so a sequence whose animal is only in frame for one image
can be scored on an empty frame. Picking one image per sequence gives a set where
every image is scored on its own.

## Inputs

- `config/awt_2026_11_by_image.yaml` (test set `awt_2026_11_by_image`).
- `config/awt_2026_11_by_image_sequences.csv`: class, tag, source env and sequence ID
  for every sequence (no camera names or timestamps).
- The source projects' realtime `media.csv`, `observations.csv` and
  `deployments.csv` (GET only, cached in `state/<set>/sources/`).
- A Camtrap DP export **with bounding boxes** of each source project, for per-image
  detector scores (`state/<set>/source_exports/`).

## Code

```{python eval=FALSE}
import subprocess
cfg = "config/awt_2026_11_by_image.yaml"
# Reuses a bounding-box export if one exists (e.g. made in the WIMP web UI); otherwise
# creates ONE (POST /projects/{id}/exports {"includeBoundingBoxes": true}), records its
# id in state/ so it is never created twice, polls until Completed and unzips it.
# Sources with `bbox_export: false` in the config are skipped.
subprocess.run(["python", "-m", "wimpbench", "source-export", "--config", cfg], check=True)
subprocess.run(["python", "-m", "wimpbench", "select-by-image", "--config", cfg], check=True)
```

Rule per sequence (images ordered by timestamp, then file name):

| Class | Pick | `pick_rule` |
|---|---|---|
| Animal classes | highest score of an `animal` media-level box | `max_animal_score` |
| Human | highest score of a `human` box | `max_human_score` |
| Vehicle | highest score of a `vehicle` box | `max_vehicle_score` |
| Blank | middle image, `(n - 1) // 2` | `middle` |
| No scored box of the right type in the sequence | middle image | `fallback_middle` |
| Source project has no bounding-box export | middle image | `middle_no_source_scores` |

Ties go to the earliest image.

## Where the detector score was found

In the bounding-box export, `observations.csv` holds media-level rows
(`observationLevel = media`) with `mediaID`, `observationType`, `bboxX/Y/Width/Height`
and `classificationProbability`. That column is the only per-image score, and it is
what we used. It is **not** a MegaDetector score for most images:

- The TEST source export has 4,115 media-level rows on 3,901 images out of 255,227,
  covering 1,039 sequences. MegaDetector's own detections are not exported. Only
  boxes stored with media-level observations are, and almost all of those are
  attributed to the human validator (`classificationMethod = human` or the
  validator in `classifiedBy`). 24 rows are from the Wet Tropics model.
- Scores are 0.60 to 1.00, with median and quartiles all 1.00, so they barely rank
  images.
- No other column or endpoint carries per-image detector scores. Event-level rows
  have `classificationProbability` but no box. The API (`/docs`) has no media-level
  detection endpoint, and `GET /sequences/{id}/observations` is event-level.
- The PROD source export could not be made: the account is Project coordinator, not
  Maintainer, on that project (POST returned 401). Its 962 sequences (881 non-blank)
  use the middle image.

## Output

`results/awt_2026_11_by_image/selection_summary.csv` (3 November 2026):

- 2,905 images, one per sequence.
- Picked by score: 23 (19 animal: 7 Felis catus, 5 Megapodius reinwardt, 4 Muridae,
  and 1 each of Alectura lathami, Perameles nasuta and Sus scrofa; plus 1 human and
  3 vehicle).
- Blank (middle image by rule): 244 (81 of them from PROD).
- Middle image because the sequence has no scored box (TEST source): 1,757.
- Middle image because the PROD source has no bounding-box export: 881 non-blank
  sequences.

So in practice this is a **middle-image** test set, not a best-image one. Detector
recall on it is not an upper bound. It sits between the by-sequence figure and what
a best-image pick would give.

`results/<set>/manifest.csv` (public): class, tag, in_model, file name.
`state/<set>/manifest_full.csv` (private, git-ignored): by-sequence columns plus
`pick_score`, `pick_rule` and `sequence_images`.

## Known issues

- The Camtrap DP export does not include MegaDetector boxes. A true best-image pick
  needs WIMP to export machine detections with their confidence (see
  `docs/upstream_suggestions.md`).
- Creating an export needs the Maintainer role on the project. An API key with a
  lower role gets 401, not 403.
- The middle image of a sequence where the animal crosses quickly can be empty, so
  some animal "misses" are frames with no animal in them.
